days.decision: The page lists 15 measurable CV checks, scores the ticked ones out of 30 by weight, shows each failed check's effect on a reader, follows the system light or dark setting, and prints on one page.
days.constraint: Has a dark mode that follows the system setting.

days.decision: The page loads with a grey example of 5 stripes under a red goal line at 8, then lets the user set a goal and tap to add one blue stripe per glass, and clears the stripes when the device date changes.
days.constraint: Shows a filled-in example before the user types.

days.decision: The page is a 560×400 px card where the user lists stretches, hold times, and a "both sides" mark, then runs the sequence by ear through three tone patterns and vibration, with a shareable link carrying the list.

The page is a one-sheet weekly planner: the user types days, exercises, sets, and reps on screen, then prints a black-and-white A4 grid with one empty circle per set and one thin orange rule under each day name.

The page tracks one goal through dated milestones, shows percent done as a plain count with its formula printed under the number, and keeps every earlier plan as a greyed, folded version whenever a date or milestone changes.
days.constraint: Shows the formula or rule behind every result.

days.task: Camping checklist grouped by shelter, cooking, clothing, and safety, printable.
days.decision: The page is an editable camping checklist that prints on 1 A4 sheet as 4 drawn panels (shelter, cooking, clothing, safety), with Out and Back tick boxes on every line and each item's weight in grams summed per panel in kilograms.
planProblems: Sisyphus speaks 4 times in the Clash, more than 3

days.decision: The page is a gray maze with a bare paper figure at its morning gate, and the visitor does one thing: drag a single thread from the gate to the evening wall, and the corridors it passes through become their timed morning and evening steps.
days.constraint: The user does exactly one thing on the page.

methods: Work in silence for the first ten minutes before any music or talk.
Swap your draft with someone else's and finish theirs.
List every material you cannot use, then start.
Design for the most frustrated possible user first.
Ask a child to explain what it is for.
Set a budget of zero and see what still works.
Translate the brief into a question, then answer only the question.
Choose the constraint you like least and keep it.
constraints: Works fully offline after the first load.
No more than two levels of heading.
tasks: Sunrise and sunset calculator: a date and coordinates entered give sunrise time, sunset time, and day length.
Color contrast checker: two colors entered give the contrast ratio and a pass or fail against a threshold the user sets.
QR code generator: text or a link entered draws a scannable code locally in the browser.
Random team generator: a list of names and a group size give randomly assigned teams.
Average calculator: a list of numbers gives the mean, median, mode, and range.
Dice and coin flip simulator: number of dice or coins and number of rolls give a results table and totals.

methods: Make ten rough versions before choosing one.
Start from the final result and work backwards.
Cut the first draft by half.
Test on paper before building anything.
Copy a structure from an unrelated field.
Work at actual size only.
Use one grid for every part.
Write the announcement before the work exists.
tasks: Bill splitter: total, tip percent, and number of people give the amount per person, rounded to 0.05, with the formula shown.
Savings goal planner: target amount, target date, and current savings give the amount to save per week and per month.
Subscription tracker: subscriptions with price and billing cycle give monthly and yearly totals, sorted by cost.
Loan repayment calculator: amount, annual rate, and term give the monthly payment, total interest, and a year-by-year table, with the formula shown.
Unit price comparer: two to five products with price and size give the cost per 100 g or per item and mark the cheapest.
Monthly budget sheet: income and up to 15 expense lines give totals and the amount left, in a layout that prints on one page.

methods: Write the instructions for a stranger, then follow them exactly yourself.
Find the most expensive possible mistake and design it out first.
Do the task by hand three times before automating any of it.
Ask what the user does just before and just after, and design for both.
Label every part with its purpose, then delete the parts with no label.
Finish one complete rough pass before polishing any single part.
Sort each decision into reversible and permanent, and slow down only on the permanent ones.
Write the help text, then change the design until the help text is not needed.
constraints: Uses no more than two font sizes.
Every result appears in a full sentence as well as a number.
tasks: Price in hours: take-home pay per hour and any price give its cost in working hours and 40-hour weeks, with a daily item also shown per year.
Estimate anything: a question split into steps, each with a low and high guess, gives a likely range for the answer, with every step shown.
Picture hanging helper: wall width, frame widths, and gap between frames give the nail position for each frame, measured from the left.
Garden bed soil calculator: bed length, width, and depth give the soil volume in litres and the number of bags of a size the user enters.
Seating plan: guests and table sizes give a printable plan, with pairs the user marks kept at different tables.
Roman numeral converter: numbers from 1 to 3,999 converted in both directions, with each step of the conversion shown.

methods: Watch three people use the current version first.
Build the smallest version that works end to end.
Remove one element per pass until it breaks, then restore the last one.
Sketch with a thick marker so small detail is impossible.
Give each idea 20 minutes, then move on.
Explain it aloud to someone outside the field.
Map every step the user takes, then remove steps.
Pick the one number that matters and design around it.
constraints: Works on a 320 px wide screen.
tasks: Freelance rate calculator: target yearly income, working weeks, hours per week, and yearly costs give the minimum hourly rate.
Debt payoff comparison: up to five debts compared by smallest balance first and highest rate first, in months and total interest.
Shared house expenses: who paid what gives who owes whom, settled with the fewest transfers.
Travel money table: a rate the user types in gives a printable table of common amounts in both currencies.
Compound growth illustration: starting amount, monthly addition, rate, and years give a year-by-year table and chart, labelled as an illustration, not a forecast.
Receipt checker: item prices, quantities, discount, and tax rate give the total to compare with a receipt.
